title: Development of an immunological IL2whole blood test for the diagnosis of active tuberculosis
summary:
Tuberculosis is still a global health problem which is proven by about 10.6 million new infections in 2022. Only 3-5% of the infected persons develop active tuberculosis. The rest of about 97 % of the infected persons remain healthy throughout their life. There is currently no immunological test which can separate the healthy but infected persons, the so-called Latent Tuberculosis Infection (LTBI) from those that are infected but suffer from active tuberculosis. This is the major problem in the area of tuberculosis diagnosis.

The aim of the current study is to test whether the newly developed test can differentiate the healthy but infected subjects from those which are infected but are suffering from active tuberculosis.

interventions.name:
It is not an intervention study

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants are exclusively informed and consenting persons who are routinely examined for a potential tuberculosis infection at Städtisches Klinikum Braunschweig. There should be no participants from specially protected groups.
Exclusion criteria:
Minors or persons unable to give informed consent.
